title: Marlowe & Finch Gift Registry Terms: Moving the Event Date
content:
**Rule.** The registrant can move the event date of a Marlowe & Finch Gift Registry while the registry is in active status, which is the last status in which a change is allowed for every registry type. The registry record must show active status when the change is made.

**Limits.** At most the registry type's allowed number of event date changes is made over the registry's life, counted by the registry's running count of event date changes. The new event date is no more than the registry type's furthest move, in full calendar months, before or after the event date first registered.

**Effect.** The completion period, the rewards payout date and the registry return window follow the new date. Once the completion period has opened, the date can no longer change, and a moved date never reopens a closed period.

### Judgement table

| Status | Changes already made | New date within the furthest move from the date first registered | Change allowed |
|---|---|---|---|
| active | fewer than the type's limit | yes | yes |
| active | equal to the type's limit | — | no |
| active | fewer than the type's limit | no | no |
| completion, closed or cancelled | — | — | no |

### Worked cases (hypothetical, for a type allowing 2 changes and 6 months)

- Event date first registered 10 May; the registry is active and shows 1 change so far. A move to 10 November of the same year lies exactly 6 full calendar months after the date first registered: allowed, and this is the second and last change.
- The same registry later asks for a third change: the count already equals 2, so no further change is made.
- A move to 11 November would lie beyond 6 full calendar months from 10 May and is not allowed, whatever date the registry currently shows.
